questions.question: Connect: Sachin Tendulkar's farewell partner on his last day; the man who scored 97 in the 2011 final; Yuvraj Singh, Player of the Tournament; Zaheer Khan opening the bowling. What event?
questions.answer: India's 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup winning squad
questions.explanation: Gambhir's 97, Yuvraj PoT, Zaheer leading the attack — the campaign Dhoni finished with the six.

questions.question: Connect: Virender Sehwag; Rahul Dravid; Sachin Tendulkar; Sourav Ganguly; VVS Laxman. What were they collectively called in the 2000s?
questions.answer: India's Test batting Fab Five (the famous middle order / top order of the 2000s)
questions.explanation: The five who dominated India's Test batting through the 2000s.

questions.question: Connect: Mithali Raj; Jhulan Goswami; Smriti Mandhana; Harmanpreet Kaur. What links them?
questions.answer: Indian women's cricket team captains / stars
questions.explanation: Mithali (most ODI runs), Jhulan (most ODI wickets), Smriti and Harmanpreet — the faces of Indian women's cricket.

questions.question: Connect: Amsterdam 1928; Berlin 1936 where a wizard scored a hat-trick in the final; London 1948 — the first post-Independence; Moscow 1980. What were these for India?
questions.answer: India's eight Olympic gold medals in field hockey
accept: hockey gold medals at the olympics
questions.explanation: Eight golds — 1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964, 1980. Dhyan Chand's hat-trick in the 1936 final.

questions.question: Connect: a Coimbatore teenager who became India's first GM in 1987; a five-time world champion who lost the title to Magnus Carlsen; an 18-year-old who beat Ding Liren in December 2024. What links Anand and Gukesh?
questions.answer: Indian world chess champions
questions.explanation: Anand (2000, 2007, 2008, 2010, 2012) and Gukesh (Dec 2024, youngest ever) — India's two world champions in chess.

questions.question: Connect: All England 1980; All England 2001; London 2012 bronze; Rio 2016 silver and Tokyo 2020 bronze. Which Indian sport?
questions.answer: Indian badminton (Padukone, Gopichand, Saina, Sindhu)
questions.explanation: Prakash Padukone, Pullela Gopichand, Saina Nehwal, PV Sindhu — the lineage.

questions.question: Connect: KD Jadhav at Helsinki 1952; Sushil Kumar with two Olympic medals; Sakshi Malik becoming the first Indian woman to medal in this sport; Bajrang Punia. Which discipline?
questions.answer: Indian wrestling (kushti) at the Olympics
questions.explanation: India's individual Olympic wrestling tradition — from Jadhav's 1952 bronze onwards.

questions.question: Connect: Rajendra Prasad serving the longest; Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, the philosopher; A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, the missile man; Droupadi Murmu since 2022. What office?
questions.answer: President of India
questions.explanation: Four of the fifteen — Prasad (1st), Radhakrishnan (2nd), Kalam (11th), Murmu (15th and current).

questions.question: Connect: B.R. Ambedkar in the chair; K.M. Munshi; Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar; N. Madhava Rau; T.T. Krishnamachari (a later addition). Which committee?
questions.answer: The Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India
accept: the drafting committee of the indian constitution
questions.explanation: The seven-member body that drafted the Indian Constitution, chaired by Ambedkar.

questions.question: Connect: Operation Polo in September 1948 brought one in; a 1947 plebiscite settled another after the Nawab fled; the Maharaja signed the Instrument on October 26, 1947 for a third. What process?
questions.answer: The accession / integration of the princely states (Hyderabad, Junagadh, Jammu and Kashmir) into India
questions.explanation: Hyderabad (Operation Polo), Junagadh (plebiscite), J&K (Maharaja Hari Singh's accession) — Patel's project.

questions.question: Connect: Nehru's 'Temple of New India' on the Sutlej; the Mahanadi project that was the world's longest earthen dam at completion; one on the Narmada that displaced many. What are these?
questions.answer: Major Indian dams (Bhakra Nangal, Hirakud, Sardar Sarovar)
questions.explanation: Bhakra Nangal (Sutlej), Hirakud (Mahanadi, Odisha), Sardar Sarovar (Narmada, Gujarat).

questions.question: Connect: Lothal in Gujarat; Dholavira in Kutch; Rakhigarhi in Haryana; Kalibangan in Rajasthan. What links these?
questions.answer: Indus Valley Civilisation sites in India (Harappan sites)
accept: indus valley civilisation sites in india
questions.explanation: The Harappan / Indus Valley sites that lie inside India (Mohenjo-daro and Harappa are in Pakistan).

questions.question: Connect: a fish; a tortoise; a boar; a man-lion; a dwarf; a warrior with an axe; an exiled prince; a cowherd. What sequence?
questions.answer: The Dashavatara — the ten avatars of Vishnu (these are the first eight)
questions.explanation: Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Narasimha, Vamana, Parashurama, Rama, Krishna — followed by Buddha and Kalki.

questions.question: Connect: Gitanjali, for which the Nobel came in 1913; Ghare Baire; Gora; Chokher Bali; the short story Kabuliwala. Whose works?
questions.answer: Rabindranath Tagore
questions.explanation: Gurudev's major works — including the novel adapted by Satyajit Ray as The Home and the World.

questions.question: Connect: Godan, the story of Hori the peasant; Gaban; Nirmala; Karmabhumi; Rangbhumi. Whose Hindi-Urdu novels?
questions.answer: Munshi Premchand
questions.explanation: The towering Hindi-Urdu novelist of the early 20th century.

questions.question: Connect: Gwalior, the oldest; Kirana, home of Bhimsen Joshi; Jaipur-Atrauli of Kishori Amonkar; Patiala of Bade Ghulam Ali Khan. What are these?
questions.answer: Hindustani classical music gharanas
questions.explanation: Major schools / lineages of Hindustani vocal music.

questions.question: Connect: Roja in 1992 — the debut; Bombay; Dil Se; Lagaan; and a 2008 British film that won two Oscars. Whose scores?
questions.answer: A.R. Rahman
questions.explanation: Mani Ratnam's discoveries through Slumdog Millionaire — Rahman won Best Original Score and Best Original Song ('Jai Ho') in 2009.

questions.question: Connect: Pancham, son of Sachin Dev; Naushad of Mughal-e-Azam fame; the duo behind Sholay's score; the duo identified with Yash Chopra romances. What craft?
questions.answer: Hindi film music directors / composers
questions.explanation: R.D. Burman, Naushad, R.D. Burman again (Sholay), Shiv-Hari / Laxmikant-Pyarelal — the architects of Hindi film music.

questions.question: Connect: Pran's menace; Amjad Khan as Gabbar; Amrish Puri as Mogambo; Kulbhushan Kharbanda as Shakaal. What role?
questions.answer: Iconic villains of Hindi cinema
questions.explanation: The great heavies — Pran the gentleman-villain, Gabbar, Mogambo, Shakaal.

questions.question: Connect: Rajinikanth; Kamal Haasan; MGR; Sivaji Ganesan. Which industry?
questions.answer: Tamil cinema mega-stars
questions.explanation: Four pillars of Tamil cinema across generations.

questions.question: Connect: Mrinal Sen; Ritwik Ghatak; Tapan Sinha; Aparna Sen. What links them (besides Satyajit Ray's shadow)?
questions.answer: Bengali / Bangla art-cinema directors (parallel cinema)
questions.explanation: The other masters of Bengali cinema beyond Ray.

questions.question: Connect: a textile salesman in Aden who came back to start Reliance Commercial Corporation; a 1977 IPO that was seven times oversubscribed; a September 2016 launch of free 4G. What house?
questions.answer: Reliance / the Ambani family / Reliance Industries
questions.explanation: Dhirubhai's polyester-to-petrochem story, his landmark IPO, and Mukesh's Jio.

questions.question: Connect: a Mumbai company started by the Tatas in 1968; a Pune company founded by seven engineers in 1981; a Bangalore company built by Azim Premji on vegetable oils; one Shiv Nadar started in 1976. What sector?
questions.answer: India's Big Four IT services companies (TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL)
questions.explanation: TCS (Tata, 1968), Infosys (Murthy + 6 others, Pune 1981), Wipro (Premji pivoted from cooking oil), HCL (Shiv Nadar, 1976).

questions.question: Connect: a Bangalore company sold to Walmart for about $16 billion in 2018; Vijay Shekhar Sharma's payments venture; Deepinder Goyal's food delivery; Bhavish Aggarwal's ride-hailing. What links them?
questions.answer: Indian unicorn start-ups (Flipkart, Paytm, Zomato, Ola)
questions.explanation: The first wave of Indian consumer-internet billion-dollar companies.

questions.question: Connect: a physicist who died in an Air India crash near Mont Blanc in 1966; the man called the father of India's space programme; the architect of Smiling Buddha in 1974; the missile man who became President. What field?
questions.answer: Architects of India's nuclear / atomic energy and space programme
accept: indian atomic and space programme leaders
questions.explanation: Homi Bhabha, Vikram Sarabhai, Raja Ramanna, A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.

questions.question: Connect: May 18, 1974 codenamed for a smiling figure; May 11 and 13, 1998 under a poet-PM with the codename Shakti. What programme?
questions.answer: India's nuclear weapons tests at Pokhran (Pokhran-I and Pokhran-II)
questions.explanation: Pokhran-I (Smiling Buddha, Indira) and Pokhran-II (Operation Shakti, Vajpayee).

questions.question: Connect: a Tamil Nadu scientist who got the Ramon Magsaysay; an American agronomist who won the 1970 Nobel Peace Prize; a Tamil Nadu agriculture minister of the mid-1960s. What did they bring?
questions.answer: The Green Revolution in India
questions.explanation: M.S. Swaminathan, Norman Borlaug, C. Subramaniam — the trio behind India's wheat turnaround.

questions.question: Connect: Alla Rakha; Zakir Hussain; Kishan Maharaj; Anokhelal Mishra. What instrument?
questions.answer: The tabla (tabla maestros)
questions.explanation: Four giants of the tabla — Alla Rakha and his son Zakir among them.

questions.question: Connect: Lata Mangeshkar; Asha Bhosle; Geeta Dutt; Shamshad Begum. What links them?
questions.answer: Female playback singers of Hindi cinema
questions.explanation: Four reigning voices of Hindi film playback across decades.

questions.question: Connect: Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan's soaring voice; the Sabri Brothers' Bhar Do Jholi; the Wadali Brothers from Punjab; Rahat Fateh Ali Khan in Bollywood. What form?
questions.answer: Qawwali (Sufi devotional music)
questions.explanation: Sufi devotional song — the Khans of Pakistan and the Wadalis of Punjab.
